shared.caseExamplesTitle: Content you can put to work
shared.caseExamplesLead: The format depends on your audience, and you make the final call. Here are examples of source material that fits each workflow.
shared.featureExamplesLead: Use the tool for practical steps in your workflow, from reviewing a recording to preparing a delivery.

automaticClips.heading: Find moments worth sharing
automaticClips.body: Start with a full recording to find segments built around a clear idea, reaction, or answer. Review the context of each suggestion, adjust its boundaries, and decide which excerpts are ready to become clips before exporting.

first.title: Interviews and podcasts
first.description: Review answers, stories, and opinions without losing the conversation behind them.

second.title: Classes and webinars
second.description: Find explanations that can become short pieces people can understand on their own.

third.title: Livestreams
third.description: Revisit plays, reactions, and conversations to choose what to share.

automaticClips.imageAlt: Editor reviewing a selected interview segment on a monitor.

subtitleEditor.heading: Make every word easy to read
subtitleEditor.body: Treat the transcript as a starting point you can review before export. Correct names, terms, or phrases, adjust the available visual style, and check that captions remain readable in the final frame.

first.title: Names and terminology
first.description: Correct names, brands, or specialist vocabulary that needs a human review.

second.title: Readable on screen
second.description: Check contrast, placement, and line length at the video’s final size.

third.title: Consistent style
third.description: Use the available design options to keep clips visually consistent.

subtitleEditor.imageAlt: Creator speaking to camera in a vertical video.

verticalExport.heading: Prepare a vertical version
verticalExport.body: Prepare vertical 9:16 clips from a horizontal recording. Review what appears inside the crop and adjust the framing in the editor when needed to keep the speaker or important detail visible.

first.title: A person speaking
first.description: Check that the face and captions stay within the visible vertical area.

second.title: Conversations
second.description: Review scenes with more than one person and reposition the frame if needed.

third.title: Social versions
third.description: Prepare vertical video for channels designed for full-screen viewing.

verticalExport.imageAlt: Widescreen interview in a blue-lit studio.

brandTemplates.heading: Keep your visual identity consistent
brandTemplates.body: Brand options help you repeat a visual treatment without starting each clip from scratch. Set up the options available for your project, use them as a reference for new pieces, and review every result before publishing.

first.title: Channel identity
first.description: Keep colors and caption style recognizable across one creator’s videos.

second.title: Client projects
second.description: Organize each project’s visual preferences using the tools in your plan.

third.title: Recurring series
third.description: Give clips in the same series or campaign a consistent presentation.

brandTemplates.imageAlt: Three presenter previews with a consistent visual identity.

latamAi.heading: Work with Spanish language content
latamAi.body: Work with interviews, classes, and livestreams in Latin American Spanish while accounting for local expressions. Review names, slang, and context-specific references: suggestions can help find cuts, and your judgment confirms the meaning is preserved.

first.title: Slang and expressions
first.description: Check that a local phrase keeps its intent when separated from the conversation.

second.title: Names and references
second.description: Verify places, people, and specific terms before sharing the transcript.

third.title: Conversational voices
third.description: Review interviews, classes, and livestreams where delivery matters as much as the words.

latamAi.imageAlt: Two people having a conversation in a podcast studio.

batchExport.heading: Prepare several deliveries together
batchExport.body: Once a selection is ready, prepare downloads for several clips in the same project in one workflow, based on the options in your plan. Review the files and formats so the final delivery stays organized.

first.title: Approved selection
first.description: Download the clips you have reviewed together for a campaign or delivery.

second.title: Multiple pieces
second.description: Skip repeated steps when you finish more than one clip in a project.

third.title: Organized handoff
third.description: Check file names and formats before sharing with your team or client.

batchExport.imageAlt: An esports livestream turned into several vertical clips.

projectManagement.heading: Keep everything in the right project
projectManagement.body: Group videos and clips by client, campaign, or topic so each delivery stays with its source. A clear structure makes it easier to return to a recording, review what has been produced, and find the right material when you need it again.

first.title: Client work
first.description: Keep each brand’s materials in its own space to avoid mixing deliveries.

second.title: Campaigns and seasons
second.description: Separate productions by initiative or period to follow content work over time.

third.title: Find a recording again
third.description: Locate the source video and related clips when you want to update a post.

projectManagement.imageAlt: Producer reviewing a library of video projects.

cliperos.heading: More time for creative judgment
cliperos.body: When you work with several creators, reviewing every full VOD takes time away from editing, creative judgment, and communication. Clipealo suggests moments from streams, interviews, and live videos; you decide which cuts fit each channel’s tone and context.

first.title: Long streams
first.description: Review gaming, Just Chatting, music, or IRL moments without searching for every cut from scratch.

second.title: Different channels
second.description: Evaluate suggestions with each creator’s personality and audience in mind.

third.title: Thoughtful delivery
third.description: Adjust the start and end, check captions, and prepare only the clips you would actually publish.

cliperos.imageAlt: Clip editor working with a phone beside the monitor.

streamers.heading: Your stream lives beyond the broadcast
streamers.body: A livestream can keep creating value after it ends. Use the recording to find standout plays, reactions, chat replies, and conversations worth sharing with a wider audience, then review every cut before posting it as a short clip.

first.title: Plays and reactions
first.description: Bring back a standout game, spontaneous reaction, or unexpected moment from a stream.

second.title: Chat conversations
second.description: Turn replies and explanations into clips that make sense beyond the full livestream.

third.title: Content between streams
third.description: Prepare posts that keep the conversation with your community going throughout the week.

streamers.imageAlt: Streamer alongside a collection of vertical reaction clips.

podcasters.heading: Make every great conversation visible
podcasters.body: An episode brings together ideas, stories, and opinions that may not reach people who prefer short-form content. Review suggested cuts, keep the question or phrase that gives them context, and adapt each excerpt for the channel where you want to share it.

first.title: Complete ideas
first.description: Choose answers that make a clear point on their own while keeping the question that prompted them.

second.title: Stories and anecdotes
second.description: Find stories, humor, or disagreement that show the personality of the conversation.

third.title: Episode series
third.description: Organize several excerpts from a recording around one topic or guest.

podcasters.imageAlt: Two people recording a podcast with microphones and cameras.

coaches.heading: A lesson can start new conversations
coaches.body: Your classes and coaching sessions contain explanations that can keep helping people after the live session. Select clips with a practical, complete idea, check that examples still make sense, and prepare a short piece for your channels.

first.title: Actionable lessons
first.description: Share a concrete explanation or recommendation an audience can remember and use.

second.title: Common questions
second.description: Turn a clear answer from a session into a useful resource for future students.

third.title: A reason to go deeper
third.description: Share an introductory idea that leads into a class, course, or follow-up conversation.

coaches.imageAlt: Educator teaching a video call lesson from his desk.

creators.heading: Get more from what you already recorded
creators.body: Your long videos already contain material for new formats. Reuse interviews, tutorials, vlogs, and conversations to explore different angles while preserving the idea’s context and reviewing every cut against your voice and style.

first.title: Interviews
first.description: Bring back concise answers that stand on their own and spark interest in the full conversation.

second.title: Tutorials and vlogs
second.description: Separate an instruction, discovery, or scene with a clear beginning and ending.

third.title: Reusable library
third.description: Return to older recordings when an idea is still useful to your audience.

creators.imageAlt: Creator recording with a phone and ring light.

communities.heading: Keep the event moments alive
communities.body: Tournaments, games, and community events create moments worth keeping. Review plays and reactions, add the context people need, and prepare a recap that invites those who missed it to join the next activity.

first.title: Tournaments and games
first.description: Select key plays, comebacks, and team moments to recap an event.

second.title: Community reactions
second.description: Highlight comments, celebrations, and participant voices with their context.

third.title: Invites and recaps
third.description: Use event moments to revisit what happened and announce the next gathering.

communities.imageAlt: Esports team and a selection of clips featuring its members.

agencies.heading: Every client in context
agencies.body: When you work with several brands, every recording needs context, review, and a clear delivery. Group material by client or campaign, assess suggested cuts against the communication goal, and adapt the result to each project’s guidelines.

first.title: One project per campaign
first.description: Keep source videos and their clips together while a delivery is being reviewed.

second.title: Review before delivery
second.description: Check the message, framing, and captions before sharing a selection with a client.

third.title: Formats by channel
third.description: Prepare the versions each platform needs using the options in your plan.

agencies.imageAlt: Client video collections organized by subject.

brands.heading: More pieces from one production
brands.body: Interviews, webinars, and events carry messages that can work across more than one channel. Find excerpts that fit the campaign, check that they preserve the brand’s meaning, and prepare each piece for approval before publishing.

first.title: Webinars and events
first.description: Reuse expert insights, announcements, and highlights from a production.

second.title: Customer and team voices
second.description: Select testimonials or explanations that add context and credibility.

third.title: Campaigns and culture
third.description: Reuse launches, demos, and workplace moments across different channels.

brands.imageAlt: Brand interview alongside conversation and event clips.
